# vaultwarden_organization_events (Data Source)

Use this data source to read the event log of an organization between two dates, such as logins, changes to items, collections, groups and members, and policy updates. The provider user needs the `Owner` or `Admin` role in the organization.

Vaultwarden only logs events when `ORG_EVENTS_ENABLED` is set to `true` on the server; otherwise this data source returns no events. Events older than `EVENTS_DAYS_RETAIN` days are deleted, if that is set.

Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The events of the last 24 hours. Needs ORG_EVENTS_ENABLED=true on the server
data "vaultwarden_organization_events" "example" {
  organization_id = "a1b2c3d4-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  start           = timeadd(plantimestamp(), "-24h")
}

# The members who exported the organization vault
output "vault_exports" {
  value = [
    for event in data.vaultwarden_organization_events.example.events : {
      date    = event.date
      user_id = event.acting_user_id
    } if event.type_name == "organization_client_exported_vault"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `organization_id` (String) The ID of the organization
- `start` (String) The start of the period to read events from, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Use `timeadd(plantimestamp(), "-24h")` for a period relative to the time of the plan

### Optional

- `end` (String) The end of the period, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to the time of the read

### Read-Only

- `events` (Attributes List) The events, newest first. IDs that do not apply to an event are `null` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--events))

<a id="nestedatt--events"></a>
### Nested Schema for `events`

Read-Only:

- `acting_user_id` (String) The ID of the user who caused the event
- `collection_id` (String) The ID of the collection the event is about
- `date` (String) When the event happened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp
- `device_type` (Number) The type of the device the event came from, as Bitwarden's device type number
- `group_id` (String) The ID of the group the event is about
- `ip_address` (String) The IP address the event came from
- `item_id` (String) The ID of the item the event is about
- `organization_user_id` (String) The ID of the organization member the event is about
- `policy_id` (String) The ID of the policy the event is about
- `type` (Number) The type of the event, as Bitwarden's event type number, such as `1300` for a created collection
- `type_name` (String) The name of the type of the event, such as `collection_created`, or the number for a type unknown to the provider
- `user_id` (String) The ID of the user the event is about
